body:
Global crypto markets took a meaningful hit on October 15, 2026, with total market cap falling to $2.73T, a decline of 5.88% over the past 24 hours. The mood is defensive across the board, and the Fear & Greed index reflects exactly that kind of pivot — dropping from 62 (Greed) yesterday to 53 (Neutral) today, a sharp single-session sentiment reset that traders should not dismiss as noise. Volume came in at a substantial $51,478B across the 24-hour window, suggesting this is an active sell-off rather than a low-liquidity drift, and BTC dominance holding at 59.5% confirms capital is rotating defensively toward the largest asset in the space while altcoins absorb the bulk of the damage.

BTC printed $80,920 on the session, off 3.21% over 24 hours and 2.12% over 7 days, generating $40.34B in volume. The $80,000 level is the line in the sand right now — CoinDesk notes Bitcoin is holding above it even as Asian equity markets dragged broader risk assets lower, and that relative resilience matters. South Korea's chip-heavy Kospi continued to plunge according to live CoinDesk coverage, pulling BTC into sympathy selling without breaking the floor. The hourly print of -0.04% suggests the immediate selling pressure has stabilized near current levels. A clean break below $80,000 on volume would be a structurally significant development; holding it while equities stabilize gives bulls a credible floor to defend.

ETH is underperforming BTC badly, down 5.82% in 24 hours and 7.37% over the week, trading at $2,362.82 on $19.2B in volume, and ETH dominance has compressed to 10.6%. The worst performers among ZIMR-tracked majors today are LINK at -6.70%, UNI at -6.55%, and ADA at -5.99%, with ADA down a brutal 12.01% on the 7-day — that is not a rotation story, that is sustained distribution. SOL at $102.01 is down 4.97% on the day and 10.63% on the week, sitting at a psychologically significant level where a breach of $100 would likely accelerate selling. The relative outperformers — if you can call them that — are BNB at -3.05% and BTC at -3.21%, which is a clear signal the market is shedding beta aggressively. One notable divergence: DOT is down only 1.31% on the 7-day versus double-digit losses almost everywhere else, though its $0.17B volume makes that reading thin and unreliable.

The macro backdrop is unambiguous in its message: Bitcoin, copper, stocks, and yields all fell today while gold rose, per CoinDesk, which is the classic risk-off configuration and removes any illusion that today's crypto move is idiosyncratic. Asian equity weakness, anchored by the Kospi rout, is the immediate catalyst, but the broader context is a market reassessing risk appetite globally. On the regulatory front, the White House crypto council chief Patrick Witt has stepped down according to Cointelegraph, introducing uncertainty at a moment when the industry was counting on executive-branch coherence on digital asset policy. Separately, Starknet has opened a vote on a potential Ethereum L2 exit over quantum risks, a technically significant governance event that adds a layer of uncertainty around the Ethereum ecosystem precisely when ETH can least afford it. The Bitget and Liquid exploits pushing Q3 crypto hacks toward $1.2B per Cointelegraph are a further sentiment drag, reinforcing the risk-off narrative for institutional allocators.

Watch the $80,000 BTC level with discipline — a sustained close below it changes the near-term thesis entirely and likely sends SOL through $100 and ETH toward the $2,200 area. The Starknet governance vote outcome is a live risk for the ETH L2 ecosystem and warrants monitoring. Witt's departure from the White House crypto council creates a policy vacuum that could accelerate or delay pending regulatory decisions, and any clarity — positive or negative — will move markets fast. On the positive side, if Asian equity markets stabilize overnight and gold retreats, the risk-off pressure on crypto lifts mechanically. The HEX situation — $160M in token selling following reports of founder Richard Schueler's arrest per Cointelegraph — is a contained but visible contagion risk for sentiment among retail participants. Any escalation in the exchange hack narrative or further macro deterioration out of Asia would be the clearest trigger for the next leg lower.
